_comment: Retrieval backends. A skill declares WHAT it needs to read; this declares HOW,
so a blocked source is a backend swap rather than a skill rewrite.
This exists because reddit-mine failed twice on a real run and the failure was
misread. Reddit served an anti-bot challenge to a logged-out agent read. That
is a RETRIEVAL-LAYER failure -- nothing about the model, the provider, or the
routing was implicated, and changing any of them would not have moved it. The
skill's job is to refuse to fabricate when retrieval fails, which it did.
'declared'    a real option, nothing here implements it yet
'blocked'     tried and does not work; the reason is recorded

agent-browse.how: Ask the model's own browsing tools to read the subreddit directly.
agent-browse.blocked_reason: Verified 2026-09-03 and 2026-09-04: Reddit serves a 'Prove your humanity' anti-bot challenge to logged-out programmatic reads. The worker correctly refused to fabricate and reported the failure both times.
agent-browse.would_fix: Nothing on the model side. This needs an authenticated or API-based path.

manual-export.how: A human reads the window and pastes threads, or exports them, into the skill's input. Slow, and it always works.
manual-export.note: The current default precisely because it has no failure mode the skill can be blamed for.

reddit-api.how: Reddit's official API with a registered script app (OAuth client credentials).
reddit-api.needs: REDDIT_CLIENT_ID and REDDIT_CLIENT_SECRET from one free Reddit OAuth app; no Reddit username/password required.
reddit-api.note: Implemented. Set the two env vars, then use retrieval_backend=reddit-api. Keep manual-export as default until credentials exist.

pushshift-style-archive.how: A third-party archive of Reddit content.
pushshift-style-archive.note: Coverage and freshness vary, and the window matters for this skill: an archive lagging the requested window silently changes what is being measured.
